pr_title: Fix: FileStream.Dispose silently fails on Dispose when disk has run out of space
pr_comments:
> Adding this call aligns the Linux behavior to throw like we already do on Windows.

I do not think this aligns the behavior on Windows. WriteFile on Windows does not guarantee that the data were physically written to disk.

@jkotas when I said align I meant we now throw in Unix as we were already doing on Windows, because we weren't doing so before (in other words, fix the bug). I will edit that sentence to avoid confusion.

I will collect some perf numbers and come back to you.

FWIW, I do not think that this is the right way to fix this. I believe that the right way to fix this is to throw from Dispose when we are disposing. FileStream.Dispose can throw for number of other I/O related reasons when we are disposing already, so one more case to throw is not a deal breaker.

I have commented on it here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/17418#issuecomment-250127128

I talked with @jkotas and I will test his suggestion to add the fix in SafeHandle. Since the change will require more careful testing, I won't have the change immediately ready so I'll close this PR for now.

The CI is hitting a bunch of unrelated issues (so far). Mainly in mono legs, where the `IsWindowsNanoServer` check fails for some reason.

Edit: I was told a fix was provided for it so I am force-rebasing the branch.
